sources.citation: Shryock, Aaron Michael. 1995. Investigating laryngeal contrasts: an acoustic study of the consonants of Musey. UCLA Working Papers in Phonetics 89 (UCLA Ph.D. dissertation), iv+117 pp.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: library print copy (Scan & Deliver or loan): WID Offsite Storage P215.U25x vol. 89 (also: hathitrust digitized, search-only (in copyright))
sources.note: No statement on Musey word stress anywhere in 124 pp; the only 'stress' mentions concern English (subglottal pressure in emphatically stressed syllables, p. 2; Keating 1984 on English stressed vs unstressed, p. 108-109). Sec. 1.3.3 'Musey Phonology' (p. 4-7): three level tones H/M/L and six contour tones (p. 5), TBU = mora, lexical tones associate right-to-left in nouns, initial-consonant class (High vs Low group) assigns default M or L and triggers low-tone delinking (p. 5-7); verbs carry grammatical tone.

Schirru, Carlo. 2005 [vol. dated 2003]. Preliminari sperimentali sulla lingua musey. Annali della Facoltà di Lingue e Letterature Straniere dell'Università di Sassari 3: 17-48.
sources.note: No stress rule. Instrumental pilot (2 male speakers, isolated words from Bertoni's list; durations, F0, intensity, F1-F3). Treats Musey as tonal with three melodic registers (B/M/A) following Platiel 1968 p.7 and Kemigo 2000; explicitly cautions about using 'accentual' categories in a tone language ('pur con la necessaria cautela nell'uso di alcune categorie nell'ambito di una lingua tonale, una focalizzazione di tipo in qualche modo accentuale (che al momento non può che considerarsi di natura fonetica...)', p. 29-30); finds no significant relation between F0/intensity slope and syllable pos…

sources.note: Nothing; preface then entries in practical orthography without tone or stress marking.

sources.citation: Shryock, Aaron. 1997. The classification of the Masa group of languages. Studies in African Linguistics 26(1): 29-62.
sources.note: Nothing; comparative classification and Proto-Masa reconstruction; notes only that noun tone is lexical and verb tone grammatical, tone not reconstructed.

sources.citation: Duncanson, Robert. 1972. Interpreting tone in the Musey language. Work Papers of the Summer Institute of Linguistics, University of North Dakota Session 16, article 3, pp. 78-99. DOI 10.31356/silwp.vol16.03
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent (full scanned grep: no 'stress', 'accent', 'prominence'). Phonology section (p. 79-80): 28 consonants in High/Low/Neutral sets, 5 vowels with length; 'Musey has three level tones and two contours, rising and falling' (p. 80); verb tone reinterpreted as a two-tone system conditioned by initial consonant class.
